about: Ten undated team photos of machine vmc1 (Royal Vision Vender, 5 shelves x 8 selections), each read slot by slot and dated against the machine's poll history, plus the two dated reference photos, in chronological order. Photo ids keep the order in which the photos were received; chronological_rank gives the time order. Slot 'rc' = shelf r (1 = top), position c (1 = left). 'stock_seen' is the front of the rail only; 'visible_units' counts units visible down the rail where they could be counted (null = not countable). Products marked 'not legible', 'likely' or 'possibly' are uncertain. Prices are shelf tags as read (price_legible false = a guess or a blurred read); most tags below shelf 1 are unreadable at the 600x800 photo resolution. A rail holds at most 7-11 units (20oz PET 7, 16oz glass 7, 16oz PET 8, 12oz can 8, 240/250ml can 11).
method: Each photo was read at full size and in zoomed crops of each shelf and tag ledge. Dating used the machine's poll history (per-slot sales, per-slot DEX prices, door-open counter): (1) legible tags against the price schedule, which changed once on 2026-09-30 15:59 ET and not again through Nov 11; (2) rails shown empty must not sell between the photo and the next door visit, and rails shown stocked should still sell or still be stocked later; (3) layout continuity between photos and the Oct 8 / Nov 9 references; (4) door-counter rises as candidate visit times. A scoring script ranked candidate times and an independent skeptic tried to refute each date. Photos 6 and 7 were refuted; they were re-examined and kept at Sep 25 on shelf-1 layout continuity (see their evidence). Phone-gallery timestamps found later for photos 9, 3 and 2 (and the Oct 8 reference) were held out as a blind check: all three fall inside the poll-history windows, and those photos' best_guess uses the gallery time. Times are US Eastern.
machine: vmc1 (Royal Vision Vender, 5 shelves x 8 selections)

photos.source: team photo, undated, dated from the poll history
evidence: Shelf-1 tags on our rails 15-18 read $4.50: the pre-Sep-30 price schedule, not the Sep 30 15:59 reprice (18 to $5.00).
Celsius fills 25-28.
38 is the only empty rail. It records no sale until the Sep 11 16:02 reading, which bounds the photo at Sep 11 16:02. A rail with no sales does not prove it was empty, so the bound is loose.
Shelf 5 fits a full, pre-run-down machine around Sep 4: 55 and 56 both sell at the Sep 4 09:16 reading.
Its layout differs most from every other photo (vitaminwater 46-48, Diet Coke 55, Gatorade 56-57), so it is the earliest photo.
The best guess is the Sep 4 11:20 door visit (first door opening after the Aug 27 counter reset). Polling was sparse before mid-September, so late August cannot be ruled out.
Skeptic check: not refuted; the end of the window was widened from Sep 4 13:14 to Sep 11 16:02.

evidence: Every shelf-1 tag on our rails reads $4.50 (including 18, which became $5.00 at the Sep 30 15:59 reprice) and shelf-2 tags read $3.50: before Sep 30 16:00.

The skeptic proposed Sep 21 12:00 to Sep 22 08:46 instead. Rejected on shelf-1 continuity: photo 9 (gallery-confirmed Sep 21 09:36) has 15 and 17 empty and photo 8 (Sep 23-24) a different shelf 1, while photos 6/7 and 4/5 have a Monster run at 15-18. Placing 6 on Sep 21 needs shelf 1 to flip 9 -> 6 -> 8 -> 4/5.
The Sep 24 11:00-12:59 alternative is ruled out by the same shelf-1 continuity: photo 8 falls in the same no-visit interval (Sep 22 08:46 to Sep 24 14:00) and shows a different shelf 1.

Confidence stays low: the alternative windows are ruled out only by the shelf-1 continuity argument above. The window itself rests on our rails 48 and 56 and the door counter (visits Sep 25 13:59 and Sep 28 09:36-10:00).
This photo is before the Sep 25 13:59 visit and before photos 4/5 (a small refill happened at that visit; see photo 4).
Skeptic check: refuted (better window Sep 21); re-examined and kept at Sep 25 for the reasons above.
